prompt: Use repeated differentiation to find the Maclaurin series of $\ln(1+x)$ up to the $x^{3}$ term, and state the values of $x$ for which the full series converges.

**(a)** Using $e^{u}=1+u+\dfrac{u^{2}}{2}+\dots$, find the first three non-zero terms of the series for $e^{-x^{2}}$. **[2]**

**(b)** Hence estimate $\displaystyle\int_0^{0.5}e^{-x^{2}}dx$. **[2]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $u=-x^{2}$: $1-x^{2}+\dfrac{x^{4}}{2}$ **(A2)**

**(b)** $\left[x-\dfrac{x^{3}}{3}+\dfrac{x^{5}}{10}\right]_0^{0.5}=0.5-0.04167+0.00313\approx0.4615$ **(M1)(A1)** (true value 0.4613)

This integral has no elementary antiderivative, which is why series are useful.
